newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU cereals experts to discuss malting barley quota.
newsitem.headline: EU cereals experts to discuss malting barley quota.

text.p: European Union cereals experts will discuss the introduction of a reduced annual-tariff quota for 30,000 tonnes of high quality malting barley on Thursday, an EU member state official said.

A vote on the quota, which has been the subject of a lengthy dispute between the United States and the EU, is scheduled to be taken at the cereals management committee following the morning meeting of experts, the official said.
The implementing regulation (537/97) would open the quota from May 15, retrospectively from June 1, 1996.
The malting barley quota has been tied to an almost two year long dispute over the introduction of a new EU rice import system allowing three month cumulative recovery of overpaid duties.
"The fact that the experts group is being asked to make a recomendation to the management committee indicates that the Commission is moving both issues forward," the offcial said.
The two items have been the subject of requests for complaints panels at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in Geneva.
Last month the farm council approved both items subject to the withdrawal of the U.S. complaints.
"We understand that the cumulative rice proposal is now before the Commission for adoption," the member state official added.
